solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Impulses to scatter rugs around Geneva

indicators.note: things that scatter are flung apart and land in a new order
around puts the scattered letters on either side of the next item

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
Geneva is an old name for gin, from the Dutch jenever

explanation.surface: Someone feels an urge to fling rugs about the Swiss city of Geneva.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva looks like the city, but it is an old word for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgings are the pushes or promptings that drive someone to act, so they are impulses.

clue.text: Severely beat economist

blocks.note: first meaning: to pound someone with the fists, an old boxing verb
second meaning: John Stuart ..., the Victorian economist and philosopher

explanation.walkthrough: To mill someone was old slang for thrashing them with fists; the economist is John Stuart Mill.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to thrash with blows, and the surname belongs to the famous political economist John Stuart.

clue.text: Number in music group having no fixed price

indicators.note: in places one item inside the letters of the group named next

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for number
a nonet is an ensemble of nine players

explanation.surface: A clue about how many players make up a band that charges no set fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for number sits after the first two letters of the nine-piece ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: Net books once had a publisher-fixed retail price; non-net goods may be sold at whatever price the seller chooses.

clue.text: Possibly us deists most like American beer?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A wry guess that believers in a distant god are especially frothy, like a US lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Suds is American slang for beer, so the frothiest thing is the most beer-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Suds is US slang for beer, and the superlative adjective describes whatever is foamiest and most like it.

clue.text: Play of canny value possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters may stand in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre review praising a production as shrewd value for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's drama about a disillusioned estate manager is a famous stage work, so it is a play.

clue.text: Joined scripture class in bad dream

indicators.note: in sets one item inside the letters that follow
bad implies the word is spoilt and its letters thrown out of order

blocks.note: RI is religious instruction, the old school subject
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A pupil enrols in a Bible class during a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the name for scripture lessons in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who have wed are united as a couple, so they have been joined.

clue.text: Check the size or take a risk?

blocks.note: first meaning: put on a garment to see whether it fits
second meaning: chance one's arm, attempt to get away with something

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the British idiom for cheekily testing how far one can push someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers testing a garment on the body and also chancing a dubious ploy to see if it works.

clue.text: Fire bad actor somewhere in Bucks

blocks.note: to fire something is to burn it
a ham is a poor, over-the-top actor

explanation.surface: Someone wants to sack a dreadful performer somewhere in the county of Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnham is a village in Buckinghamshire, known for Burnham Beeches woodland, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: Containers for small sharp instruments require the French to take action

blocks.note: to require something is to need it
le is a French word for the
cases are actions brought in a court of law

explanation.surface: French folk are urged to do something, oddly about sewing kits.
explanation.walkthrough: Cases are lawsuits, the actions one takes against someone in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle cases are small holders that keep sewing pins and needles safe, so they contain small pointed tools.

clue.text: Foreigners in South Africa finally invest in laundries all over the place

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word it governs
something all over the place is scattered, so the combined letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the last letter of invest
taken as written, then shuffled with the extra letter

explanation.surface: Outsiders in South Africa put money into launderettes everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes into the laundries before the whole lot is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Uitlanders was the Afrikaans term for British and other outsiders working in the Boer republics, so it means foreigners there.

clue.text: Storyteller heard on musical instrument

indicators.note: heard means we go by how a word sounds when spoken

blocks.note: a storyteller in the sense of one who tells fibs

explanation.surface: A bard is heard performing on a harp.
explanation.walkthrough: To tell stories is to tell lies, so the storyteller is a fibber.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a small ancient stringed harp, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Where is it at? Among elderly aroused

indicators.note: among places the preceding words inside the word that follows

blocks.note: elderly people are aged
surface padding that turns the phrase into a question
taken as written from the question

explanation.surface: Old people get worked up asking where it is all happening.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the words it at go inside; 'Where is' is surface dressing that frames the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agitated is stirred up, disturbed or excited, so they have been aroused.

clue.text: Old man, not dead, tried playing passages with rapid repeats, …

indicators.note: not dead tells us to drop the letter that stands for dead
playing suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for dead
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man attempts to perform musical passages full of quick repetitions.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue in the surface only. Tremolando passages repeat a note rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolandi is the Italian plural of tremolando, a musical passage played with fast reiteration of notes, hence rapid repeats.

clue.text: One coveting space — rival takes room initially

indicators.note: initially keeps only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space
to rival is to vie
the first letter of room

explanation.surface: Someone jealous of a neighbour's spacious home watches a competitor grab the room.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: An envier is a person who feels envy, wanting what someone else has, so is one who covets.

clue.text: Old author and pop star about right way to ruin the earth

indicators.note: about means the preceding names wrap round the next item

blocks.note: Daniel Defoe, writer of Robinson Crusoe
Sting, singer of the Police
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A novelist and a rock singer debate how best to wreck the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for right sits between the O and E of the joined names.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing forests strips the land of trees and damages ecosystems, so deforesting is a means of harming the planet.

clue.text: … produced a harmonic and unusually low breve

indicators.note: unusually implies the letters are set in an uncommon order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a player sounds an overtone on an oddly deep long note.
explanation.walkthrough: A breve is a long note, which keeps the musical surface going.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing hard into a wind instrument makes it jump to an upper partial, so a player who overblew sounded a harmonic.

clue.text: One with incomplete alias could become windy

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its last letter
could become suggests the letters may turn into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
alias without its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone using a half-finished false name might turn into a windbag.
explanation.walkthrough: One is used whole as letters, not as the numeral or A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeolus was the Greek god of winds, so Aeolian means of or produced by the wind, hence windy.

clue.text: Temptress getting flowers after teaching

indicators.note: after tells us the flowers come behind the teaching, so the clue order is swapped

blocks.note: lore is learning handed down
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A seductress receives a bouquet after a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the flowers second, behind the teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren whose song lured boatmen to their doom, so she is a seductive temptress.

clue.text: Got up to secure record with ease

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: rose means got up out of bed or a chair
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone dressed up to grab a disc without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' can suggest dressed, but here it means stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of rest and relaxation, so it is a synonym for ease as a noun.

clue.text: Fruit for Spanish lawyers

blocks.note: first meaning: the pear-shaped green fruit
second meaning: the English fruit name came via Spanish abogado, a lawyer, close to the old spelling

explanation.walkthrough: The Aztec word for the fruit was altered in Spanish into abogado, meaning advocate, which English took up; the clue plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit name and the Spanish word for advocates share a history, Spanish speakers reshaping the Nahuatl word as their term for lawyers.

clue.text: At one’s peak playing baby grand?

blocks.note: a show that is playing is on
a baby boy is a son
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A pianist is in top form performing on a small grand piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Baby grand is a type of piano, but it splits into two pieces here; a grand is slang for a thousand pounds, written G.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom on song describes someone performing at their very best, so it means at the height of form.

clue.text: From there one’s able to return

definitions.text: From there one’s able to return

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about a place one can come back from.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon escaped from this island and returned to France, echoing the palindrome 'Able was I ere I saw Elba'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island and famously escaped back to France, so it was a place he could come home from.

clue.text: At first bather could be desperate when up to her chest

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of the word it governs
could be suggests the letters may form something else

blocks.note: the first letter of bather
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer grows frantic as the sea rises to her chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Water at that height reaches the bosom of someone wading, so the hyphenated adjective means as high as the chest.

clue.text: University fellow active in study

indicators.note: in puts one item inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a den is a private study
A is the abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A college don busy at work in his study.
explanation.walkthrough: A for active is a grammar abbreviation, as in active voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior college official, often a fellow in charge of discipline or a faculty.

clue.text: Less punctual time traveller that is right for island

indicators.note: for means one item is put in place of another

blocks.note: the TARDIS is Doctor Who's time machine
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right
Is is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A time traveller arrives late and gets directions to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the time machine in the BBC series Doctor Who; its final IS (island) is swapped for IE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardy means late, so the comparative tardier describes someone arriving later, hence less punctual.

clue.text: Take sienna and make it madder

indicators.note: make it suggests the letters are worked up into something new

blocks.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter's recipe: take the pigment sienna and turn it into madder red.
explanation.walkthrough: Sienna and madder are both artists' pigments, so madder looks like a dye, not more insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder is the comparative of mad, meaning crazier, and insaner is its synonym as a comparative adjective.
